name: MEXICAN TRAIN
description: Mexican Train is a popular domino game played mainly in the USA. It is best for four or more players and uses a double-twelve domino set. Players build trains of dominoes from a central hub, with each player having their own personal train and a shared 'Mexican Train' that anyone can play on. The game combines strategic tile placement with careful hand management.

content.text: Mexican Train is a popular domino game played mainly in the USA. It is best for four or more players and uses a double-twelve domino set. Players build trains of dominoes from a central hub, with each player having their own personal train and a shared 'Mexican Train' that anyone can play on. The game combines strategic tile placement with careful hand management.
Mexican Train originated in the United States, though its exact origins are unclear. Despite the name, it has no confirmed connection to Mexico. The game became popular in the late 20th century.
Double-twelve domino set (91 tiles with 0-12 pips on each half).
Double-twelve domino set, train markers (coins or special markers), central hub piece (optional).
Number of tiles varies by player count: 2 players = 15 each, 3-4 players = 12 each, 5-6 players = 10 each, 7-8 players = 9 each. Remaining tiles form the boneyard.

items.text: No Double Rule: Some variants don't require satisfying doubles immediately.
Long First Turn: Some variants allow playing as many dominoes as possible on the first turn.
Positive Scoring: Winner scores points for tiles played rather than opponents' penalty points.
